baselineAndRemoteState.alignmentMethod: Verified remote tree first; advanced the existing branch/index without checkout, reset, clean, or worktree replacement.

questions.question: Was an external baseline saved before repository edits?
questions.answer: Yes. The baseline contains 93 nonignored paths and the initial shallow/misaligned Git status.

questions.question: Was local state reconciled with the remote without overwriting user content?
questions.answer: All 93 local nonignored paths matched the cdb0 remote tree by Git blob and mode; the existing branch/index were aligned without checkout, reset, or clean.

questions.question: What are the current branch, PR, and workflow states?
questions.answer: Branch tip is cdb0de33; PR #1 is OPEN/DRAFT against main; push package and WARP runs succeeded, while PR Windows package and Level B jobs were skipped.

questions.question: Were the current hosted Windows executable candidate and smoke diagnostics recovered?
questions.answer: No. Both exact artifact IDs exhausted two distinct routes in M16; M17 did not repeat the exhausted attempts.

questions.question: Were artifact provenance and bytes independently verified before inspection or execution?
questions.answer: GitHub run and artifact metadata are available, but no local archive bytes or locally computed matching digest are available. Nothing was extracted or executed.

questions.question: Was a clean Windows build performed through authorized infrastructure?
questions.answer: The latest push run for the exact tested commit used a fresh windows-latest runner and passed npm ci, native/package build, EXE size validation, packaged smoke, and Level A validation. No manual dispatch was used; this does not prove bit-for-bit reproducibility.

questions.question: Did the packaged browser pass its bounded Level A smoke?
questions.answer: The hosted Windows packaged smoke process and Level A evidence validator reported success. The candidate itself was not locally downloaded or executed.

questions.question: Did the packaged independent WebGPU known-answer compute probe pass?
questions.answer: The optional Level A validator can accept PASS or a safe SKIPPED state; the per-run report is unavailable, so neither state is asserted.

questions.question: Did the packaged bundled-scene WebGPU FSR1 EASU/RCAS path pass?
questions.answer: The source implements the bounded game-owned path, but the exact packaged adapter, shader, pipeline, dispatch, dimensions, and visible-output diagnostics were unavailable.

questions.question: What does the separate D3D12/WARP processing job establish?
questions.answer: The native harness workflow reports a successful one-frame D3D12 WARP software run and keeps physical-GPU status NOT RUN; its artifact content remains unavailable for independent review.

questions.question: Was the packaged capturePage PNG to D3D12 WARP diagnostic independently inspected?
questions.answer: No. The Level A workflow step passed, but its per-run JSON and PNGs were inside the unavailable diagnostics artifact.

questions.question: Was an authorized physical-GPU runner available and was Level B run?
questions.answer: The Level B job was skipped on push/PR; the read-only runner-list API returned HTTP 403. Runner availability remains unknown. No dispatch or provisioning occurred.

questions.question: Is the Windows binary bit-for-bit reproducible?
questions.answer: No reproducibility claim: Windows toolchain versions and local executable bytes are unavailable, and there is no second independent executable hash.

questions.question: Does the app upscale ordinary arbitrary web pages?
questions.answer: Ordinary tabs remain standard Chromium WebContentsView instances. The bundled scene owns its target and does not establish arbitrary-page processing.

questions.question: What architecture options are feasible and recommended?
questions.answer: Retain the bounded game-owned WebGPU scene. Treat Electron offscreen shared texture as an unvalidated Windows prototype, Chromium/Viz integration as a costly long-term route, and user-selected image/local video as narrower scope. Do not inject into arbitrary pages.

questions.question: Is DLSS Super Resolution or Frame Generation implemented?
questions.answer: No Streamline/native renderer integration, production runtime, application identifier, or genuine DLSS output exists in the app.

questions.question: What is the M15 Images decision and current dependency/security posture?
questions.answer: Images remains deferred by default pending original M8/M9 source or explicit new scope. Source-level Electron safeguards were reviewed; full npm audit fails with eight moderate records from one sprintf-js advisory; the high-only threshold passes.

questions.question: Is release readiness established and what is the next milestone?
questions.answer: No. Exact packaged evidence, physical-GPU validation, artifact integrity, dependency risk disposition, and release-trigger review remain open. Recommend M18 Windows Acceptance Closure, then a separate architecture proof only if all-page processing is explicitly required.
